itens.titulo: Dólar hoje cai mais de 1,6%, a R$ 5,81, com especulações sobre ministro da Fazenda
itens.descricao: Dólar hoje cai mais de 1,6%, a R$ 5,81, com especulações sobre ministro da Fazenda InfoMoney
trechos: Publicidade O dólar à vista virou para queda após abrir com alta perante o real nesta quarta-feira (25), na contramão do avanço da moeda norte-americana ante outras divisas de emergentes no exterior.
O núcleo do PCE subiu 0,3%, dentro do esperado, enquanto o PIB avançou 4,3%, bem acima dos 3,4% projetados por analistas.
Às 16h04, o dólar à vista caia 1,54%, a R$ 5,820 na venda.
O dólar futuro para dezembro — o mais líquido no mercado brasileiro — avançava 0,38% na B3, aos R$ 5,932.
O que esperar após moeda atingir máxima em 18 meses?
Na terça-feira o dólar à vista encerrou a sessão com queda de 0,35%, aos R$5,9085.
Continua depois da publicidade Dólar comercial - Compra: R$ 5,819 - Venda: R$ 5,820 O que aconteceu com dólar hoje?

Na terça-feira o dólar à vista encerrou a sessão com queda de 0,35%, aos R$5,9085, em meio a notícias de que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva teria autorizado o envio ao Congresso de uma proposta que tratará de despesas obrigatórias.

itens.titulo: JPMorgan Sees S&P 500 At 8,200 In 2027 As AI Supercycle Remains Intact
itens.descricao: JPMorgan Sees S&P 500 At 8,200 In 2027 As AI Supercycle Remains Intact Yahoo Finance
trechos: - JPMorgan expects S&P 500 earnings growth to moderate to around 17% in 2027 from approximately 35% this year.

JPMorgan expects the S&P 500 to climb to 8,200 by the end of 2027, as the firm sees the artificial intelligence (AI) investment cycle continuing despite mounting concerns about spending, valuations and interest rates.
The target implies nearly 14% upside from the index's Tuesday close.

"We remain of the view that the AI supercycle remains intact with demand for compute still strong and sticky," CNBC reported, citing a note by Dubravko Lakos-Bujas, JPMorgan's head of global markets strategy.
The S&P 500 was down over 2% on Wednesday, on track for its ninth decline in the last 10 sessions.
Fed Risks And Slower Earnings Growth JPMorgan expects S&P 500 earnings growth to moderate to around 17% in 2027 from approximately 35% this year.
The Federal Reserve's more hawkish stance has raised the possibility of further interest rate hikes in 2027.
Still, Lakos-Bujas believes the S&P 500 can withstand a modest round of hikes as long as the Fed remains focused on economic growth.

itens.titulo: Bad News for Exxon and Chevron: Goldman Sees Brent Falling “Roughly $10” Next Year on a Supply Glut
itens.descricao: Bad News for Exxon and Chevron: Goldman Sees Brent Falling “Roughly $10” Next Year on a Supply Glut Yahoo Finance
trechos: Key Takeaways - Goldman Sachs expects Brent and WTI crude to fall about $10 over the next year on an oil surplus of about 2 million barrels a day.
- Each $1 move in Brent is worth about $700 million of yearly earnings to ExxonMobil and about $600 million to Chevron.
Brent has fallen more than $20 a barrel this month as the Iran war winds down, and it traded around $92 on Wednesday.

He said Goldman's "base case looks for a roughly $10 decline in Brent and WTI prices over the next year as we believe the market is likely going to be in a 2MBD, roughly 2% surplus." Not great if you own oil stocks.
Exxon's estimates have room to fall ExxonMobil's annual report says each $1 change in Brent moves its yearly earnings by about $700 million.
So Goldman's $10 drop would cost about $7 billion a year, roughly $1.70 a share, or nearly 14% of the $12.49 analysts expect Exxon to earn in 2027.
Analysts expect Exxon's normalized EPS to nearly double this year and stay high for years: Exxon earned $6.99 a share on that basis in 2025, when its realized Brent price averaged $69.06.
Even the $10.33 analysts expect for 2028 is nearly 50% higher.
